newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Wilson& Horton sees improved performance.
newsitem.headline: Wilson& Horton sees improved performance.

text.p: New Zealand newspaper group Wilson & Horton Ltd, 85 percent owned by Tony O'Reilly's Independent Newspapers, expects an improved performance in the 1997/98 year.
Chairman Liam Healy told shareholders at the annual meeting said on Thursday that the group expected to show an improved performance in the coming year.
He said that the group's Radio Network Group had met its first quarter target.
Radio Network is owned by a consortium comprising Wilson & Horton, Australian Provincial Newspapers and U.S.-based Clear Channel Communications.
Healy said the year had started well in Auckland with its flagship paper The New Zealand Herald experiencing good growth in pagination levels.
"Advertising growth across the rest of the country and in the magazine and commercial areas has been a little less strong," Healy said.
The New Zealand dollar and the high interest rates had likewise impacted on confidence and consumer spending and there had consequently been little growth in employment.
"As a result, the employment advertising is at relatively low levels."
Healy said considerable work had gone into the establishment of a Wilson & Horton internet site.
The project was nearing completion and would be commissioned soon.
Healy said newsprint pricing had stabilised some 16 percent below last year's levels, reducing some cost pressures that had been felt by all publishers.
New Zealand's new coalition government, formed in December, gave rise to an expectation of increased government spending and a resulting lift in consumer confidence and the retail market, he said.

"That confidence has not flowed through at this stage. The delay in implementation of the expected tax cuts whilst the superannuation debate is held also further dampened consumer spending," Healy said.
The site would bring the group all the advantages of the cutting edge of modern communications and will project our presence into the global market.
He said it would also enable all the company's divisions the ability to offer additional services.
